protections: Server-side outbound fetches of a client-supplied URL must not reach internal/private/loopback hosts, including via redirects or re-resolution (destination allow/deny check on every hop).

evidence: src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:6-11 (POST takes raw request body as URL and fetches it with no host check, returns body and headers)
src/services/tool.ts:17 and src/services/file/client.ts:23 (client callers send arbitrary URLs to /api/proxy)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a hostname/IP check on the submitted URL looks complete; fetch() following redirects is default behaviour and not visible in the code
evidence: src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:9 (fetch(url) with no redirect option, so redirects are followed to whatever host the 3xx names; a first-hop-only check misses it)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: resolving the hostname and checking the resulting IP before fetching looks sufficient; the second resolution inside fetch is implicit
evidence: src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:9 (fetch receives the URL string, not a pinned address, so any pre-check resolves separately from the connection)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: route looks dead: no client code references it and half the file is a commented-out copy
evidence: src/app/api/files/image/route.ts:7 (fetch(url) on a client-supplied JSON url, no auth, no host check)
src/app/api/files/image/route.ts:16-18 (fetched bytes uploaded to Imgur, so the response leaves the server)
src/app/api/files/image/route.ts:28-42 (commented-out duplicate, which supports the 'dead code' dismissal)
src/services/_url.ts:18 (client endpoint map lists /api/proxy; grep finds no reference to files/image in src)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: custom provider endpoint is a product feature, and local Ollama at 127.0.0.1 is a must-keep-working value
evidence: src/app/api/chat/agentRuntime.ts:35,45,63,96,111 (baseURL = payload?.endpoint || <server env>; client-supplied endpoint wins over server default)
src/app/api/chat/auth/utils.ts:12-17 (NON_HTTP_PREFIX tokens are decoded without verification, so payload.endpoint is fully client-controlled)
src/services/ollama.ts:10 and src/locales/default/modelProvider.ts:135 (default/placeholder Ollama endpoint is http://127.0.0.1:11434, the coupled loopback value)
src/config/server/provider.ts:202 (server-side OLLAMA_PROXY_URL env, which must keep working when it points at a private host)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: same custom-endpoint feature as chat, reached through a header instead of the JWT payload
evidence: src/const/fetch.ts:17 (endpoint read from OPENAI_END_POINT request header)
src/app/api/openai/stt/route.ts:19, src/app/api/openai/tts/route.ts:13, src/app/api/openai/images/route.ts:11 (three routes reach it)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: plugins are meant to call arbitrary third-party (and localhost dev) servers; the fetch lives in an external package
evidence: src/app/api/plugin/gateway/route.ts:63 (client-posted manifest is destructured from the request body)
src/app/api/plugin/gateway/route.ts:73 (request with that manifest handed to @lobehub/chat-plugins-gateway handler)
src/features/PluginDevModal/UrlManifestForm.tsx:108 (localhost dev plugin is a supported use)

masking: T2 and T3 only show up once T1 has a destination check: with no guard, the redirect and re-resolution routes are redundant

conflicts.what: a shared 'block private/loopback destinations' helper applied to provider endpoints breaks the 127.0.0.1:11434 Ollama default and a private OLLAMA_PROXY_URL (src/services/ollama.ts:10, src/config/server/provider.ts:202)
blocking private hosts in /api/proxy or the gateway breaks localhost plugin manifests when useProxy is on (src/features/PluginDevModal/UrlManifestForm.tsx:79-80,108)

fairness_risks: Custom provider endpoints (T5/T6) are a documented feature; treating client-supplied endpoints as SSRF is a policy choice the advisories do not state. Hidden tests would need to keep server-env private endpoints working while refusing client-supplied private ones.

Local plugin development fetches http://localhost manifests through /api/proxy (src/features/PluginDevModal/UrlManifestForm.tsx:108, src/services/tool.ts:17). A strict private-IP rule on the proxy refuses this legitimate shape.
Proxied redirects to public hosts must keep working (plugin manifests and image URLs often redirect). If T2 is fixed by refusing all redirects instead of checking each hop, legitimate use breaks.

design.why: Three independent fix sites with different reasons to dismiss. T1 is the advisory route, and its group carries the how-type redirect/re-resolution shapes (T2/T3) from B. T4 is a deepseek-type unauthenticated duplicate fetch-and-exfiltrate route that looks dead. T5 is a mimo-type coupled value: client-supplied endpoints must be restricted while loopback Ollama via server config keeps working. T6 is left out because it is the same concept as T5 by another route (easy). T7 is left out because its sink is in an external package and the plugin design contradicts a deny rule.

unverified: Fix A (465665a73555) content is not in the pinned tree; the pinned /api/proxy has no guard (src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:6-11). That A added a DNS-lookup + ip.isPrivate check is from memory, not read.

That B (e960a23b0c69) concerns redirect-following and/or a flawed private-IP check (possibly via the 'ip' package's isPrivate, CVE-2024-29415) and was fixed with a safe-fetch wrapper is not verified from code; 'ip' is not in package.json at the pinned commit.
@lobehub/chat-plugins-gateway is not installed in the worktree (no node_modules), so the gateway's actual outbound fetch for T7 is not read.
Whether a deployed instance exposes /api/files/image (T4) without Imgur config failing first was not checked (src/app/api/files/image/imgur.ts not read).
